changes.after: A for loop visits each item in a sequence. Here the sequence contains valid positions of the input.

before: for (index in seq_along(values)) visits each valid position of this vector. It does not require a separate manual counter update.
seq_along(numeric(0)) is an empty index sequence. The colon operator makes a sequence including both endpoints. Thus 1:length(values) becomes 1:0 for empty input, which is not an empty sequence.

numeric(length(values)) can allocate a result vector before a loop. Avoid repeatedly growing large vectors without measuring the cost.

For a nonnegative whole-number n, numeric(n) creates a double vector of length n initialized to zero. In particular numeric(0) creates no entries, which is why the quiz's seq_along loop has no iterations.
```r
cat(length(numeric(0)), "\n", sep = "")
cat(numeric(2), sep = ",")
```
It prints:
```text
0
0,0
```
count <- count + 1 updates the local count once per iteration. The starting zero remains zero if the sequence is empty.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
values <- c(2, 4)
count <- 0
for (index in seq_along(values)) {
  count <- count + 1
}
cat(count)
```
